title: Assigning to a key on an uninitialized local variable autovivifies an array

ground_truth.statement: In PHP, assigning to an array key on an uninitialized local variable ($result['offset'] = $offset) autovivifies $result as an array without emitting an E_WARNING or E_NOTICE, and subsequent reads/writes produce the expected array{offset: int, limit: int}.

notes: PHPStan 2.3.1 accepts array-offset autovivification cleanly. Mago 1.60.2 (as well as 1.54.0, 1.57.0, and 1.59.0) reports undefined-variable, mixed-array-assignment, mixed-array-access, mixed-argument, and mixed-return-statement (falling back to mixed rather than never/no-value). Psalm 6.20.1 reports PossiblyUndefinedVariable, InvalidReturnType, and InvalidReturnStatement.
